question: Does every reader, section and site treat this the same way?
Does the new rule contradict any existing rule, text, or test?
What existing behaviour or guarantee does this lose or undermine?
What does a background pass or read see mid-action?
Which steps must be atomic, and what lock serialises them?
What clears this marker or stale state, and when?
What bounds each wait, timer or retry, and when does it restart?
Exactly which kinds, members or records does the rule include?
Does the description cover every rule, risk, and exception?
What happens to a record that is replaced, redone or archived?
Who performs each step, and who picks up the hand-off?
What state remains if an operation fails partway?
Does stored state or a counter survive a restart or replay?
When several candidates apply, which wins and in what order?
Which identity does each stored or printed value refer to?
